summary: Halyard template mutual NDA with largely cosmetic counterparty edits (US spelling, entity details, contractors added to Representatives) plus requests to cut survival to 2 years and change governing law to Delaware/New York.

findings.quote: [[INS: VERIDIAN CLOUD, INC.]]
findings.why: The counterparty has inserted its own entity name, jurisdiction and address (a US entity), which the lawyer must confirm against the company register.

findings.quote: Disclosing Party means the Party that discloses, or procures the disclosure of, Confidential Information to the other Party under or in connection with this Agreement.
findings.why: Disclosing and Receiving Party are defined by role so either Party can be either, and the obligations bind both equally.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: Definition covers information disclosed in connection with the Purpose that is marked or reasonably confidential and includes derived notes and analyses, for either party.

findings.quote: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, which is discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship.

findings.quote: is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: All four carve-outs (public domain, already held, third-party receipt, independent development) are present, with a written records or reasonable evidence standard.

findings.quote: [[INS: independent contractors,]]
findings.why: The counterparty adds independent contractors to Representatives, a category the playbook does not list, widening who may receive Halyard information (still subject to need-to-know and liability in clause 4).
findings.draft_redline: Representatives means, in relation to a Party, the employees, officers, directors, professional advisers, auditors and insurers of that Party and of any member of its Group.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would prefer to keep the list of Representatives as drafted. If contractors need access for the Purpose, please tell us who and we can consider it case by case.

findings.quote: The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know such Confidential Information in order to evaluate or further the Purpose
findings.why: Disclosure is permitted to Representatives (including advisers, auditors, insurers) and Group members on a need-to-know basis, with the recipient liable for them.

findings.quote: take all reasonable steps requested by the Disclosing Party (at the Disclosing Party's cost) to resist or narrow the scope of the required disclosure
findings.why: Disclosure is permitted where required by law, court, regulator or stock exchange; notice only where legally permitted; resistance is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Ten Business Day return or destroy period, officer-signed confirmation, and clause 6.2 and 6.3 allow automated backup and legally required copies which stay confidential.

findings.quote: other than the limited right to use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose in accordance with the terms of this Agreement
findings.why: Confidential Information and IP stay with the Disclosing Party and the only licence is use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: Neither Party makes any representation or gives any warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy, completeness, adequacy or fitness for a particular purpose of any Confidential Information
findings.why: Information is provided as is with a mutual no-warranty disclaimer, a fraud carve-out in 7.4 and a no-obligation-to-proceed clause in 7.5.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Only business contact details are anticipated and any other personal data requires a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party
findings.why: Agreement term is 2 years with 30 days' notice to terminate early, as preferred.

findings.quote: Would Halyard be open to reducing this from 3 years to 2 years?
findings.why: The counterparty asks to cut general survival from 3 to 2 years while keeping Trade Secrets protected, which falls within the 2 to 5 year range.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek injunctive and equitable relief, with remedies cumulative under 11.2.

findings.quote: our strong preference is to govern this NDA under the laws of the State of Delaware or the State of New York, or alternatively to leave governing law and venue silent for the NDA stage
findings.why: The counterparty requests Delaware or New York law, or silence on law and venue, instead of the preferred law of England and Wales.
findings.draft_redline: This Agreement and any dispute or claim (including non-contractual disputes or claims) arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter or formation shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to agree to Delaware or New York law, or to leave governing law silent. As a compromise we can offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction, so that either party may bring proceedings in other courts.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: Exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales is the preferred position.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party
findings.why: Mutual restriction on assignment without prior written consent.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: [[INS: (such as DocuSign or Adobe Sign)]]
findings.why: Counterparts and electronic signature are already permitted; the insertion only names example platforms.
